context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Thirst, completion, a pierced side, and cited Scripture” preserves a distinct parallel witness source unit within death witness.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Jesus speaks of thirst and completion, dies, then soldiers inspect bodies, leave his legs unbroken, and pierce his side.
observations.label: Thirst, completion, a pierced side, and cited Scripture: textual observation

observations.body: The narrator interrupts the action to insist that the one who saw has testified truthfully.
observations.label: Thirst, completion, a pierced side, and cited Scripture: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Two separate Scripture statements follow two distinct bodily observations.
observations.label: Relationships named in John 19:28–37

payload.posture: Read John 19:28–37 as its own death, signs, and witnesses crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The body is unmistakably dead while the narration keeps bodily evidence, eyewitness claim, and cited Scripture distinct.
payload.title: Thirst, completion, a pierced side, and cited Scripture
